artifact: physical_page_return - rule registration for FUTURE trials
amended_at: 2026-10-24T18:55+08:00 (exact per-trial ratios recomputed from bytes; host-pool-state clauses added after the free-only decomposition was measured)
registered_by: the batch driver, on the operator's standing instruction that a metric change must be registered before the runs it scores
applies_to: page-return trials whose run is STARTED AFTER this timestamp, on any candidate
does_not_apply_to: os5 / os5b / os5c (83a880..., this batch) - these were scored one-trial-at-a-time under the pre-existing rule and keep exactly those verdicts
reason_for_registering: Three trials of the SAME executable (83a88048569f...) landed on both sides of A5: os5 0.517308 PASS (+299,436,164 B), os5b 0.499115 BLOCKED (-15,300,440 B), os5c 0.496538 BLOCKED (-59,897,700 B). Ratio spread 0.020771, margin spread 359,333,864 B. A single trial at the 0.50 line is therefore not decisive evidence about a binary.

For scale: os4's failure margin on the previous candidate was -6,920,060 B, i.e. 4.9x smaller than the spread produced by repeating the SAME binary. Candidate-level differences are currently inside trial noise for this metric.

The methodological concern that free+inactive over-credits the kernel was TESTED against the stored bytes (evidence/os_page_return_free_only_exploratory.json) and is NOT supported: the inactive component contributes at most 0.0033 of the scored gain, because inactive DRAINS (~13 GiB -> ~5 GiB) while free fills (~0.15 GiB -> ~16.2 GiB). free-only would score 0.997-0.998 on the same records, i.e. it is the LOOSER reading, not the stricter one.

binding_rule_unchanged.A5: host gain of (free+inactive) across the pre-registered settle window >= 0.5 * kernel resident drop, compared in integer bytes
binding_rule_unchanged.note: nothing in A1-A9 is relaxed; the exit teardown remains measured and excluded (exit_teardown_used_for_verdict=false)

new_binding_requirements_for_future_clai: three independent trials on that exact executable sha256, each judged by the unchanged A1-A9 set; the gate may only be reported as supported when ALL THREE pass A5
report per-trial ratio recomputed from bytes, the minimum ratio, and the margin in bytes to 0.5*drop - never the 3-decimal verdict field alone
record the free-only ratio and the inactive share of the gain beside every trial, explicitly as non-binding observations
record the host pool state at the anchor (free, inactive, free+inactive bytes) for every trial and report it beside the verdict, because the measured gain is peak minus that anchor

the host starting state may not be selected for: no re-run until a favourable anchor is found, no waiting for a 'quiet' machine, no discarding a trial because its anchor looked unusual - every started trial is kept and counted
no other memory-heavy process may run inside a trial window; if one did, the trial is recorded as contaminated and does not count toward the set of three
any trial whose candidate sha256 differs from the claimed identity invalidates the whole set

explicitly_not_adopted_here.free_only_criterion: measured as LOOSER (0.997-0.998 vs 0.4965-0.5173 on the same records), so adopting it after BLOCKED trials would move the goalpost in the passing direction. It stays a non-binding observation. If the operator wants a criterion that separates 'the target's pages' from 'the pre-existing inactive backlog', that is a new rule and must be registered, with its own threshold and repeat policy, before the runs it scores.
explicitly_not_adopted_here.lowering_the_0.50_threshold: not proposed and not done; the observed 0.5 split argues for more trials, not for a softer line
explicitly_not_adopted_here.host_state_normalisation: not attempted as a correction factor; it is recorded and reported instead, because inventing a normalisation after seeing five trials would be fitting the data

consequence_for_this_batch: physical_page_return stays BLOCKED. os5's PASS is not promoted to a candidate-level claim, because the same binary produced two BLOCKED trials and the 3-trial policy above was not in force for them.
